elaine (sales): Hey team — enterprise prospect just landed a 12-month commit but expects 3x traffic spikes during marketing events. They want a recommended capacity plan (reserved GPUs + autoscale/spot hedge), a rough pricing example we can quote, and answers for the security questionnaire items around prewarming and KMS. Can we sketch a playbook?

samir (solutions): quick thought: reserve baseline for 95th p90 sustained throughput, expose burst credits for event spikes, and enable spot-backed burst nodes with automatic fallbacks to hosted model variants.

jia (infra): Agree. Need to know target p90 latency SLO and model choice to map GPUs -> throughput. AZ affinity and cross-az failover also matters for prewarm time.

elaine (sales): Customer SLO = 99% <= 250ms token-latency for chat completions, model = LlamaX-34B quantized. They expect average concurrent sessions ~700, peak concurrent ~2100 for short bursts (~20min).

marc (eng-runtime): LlamaX-34B quantized on A100-ish nodes: rough ballpark is ~12–16 tokens/ms per GPU for short seqs; practical throughput for completions workload -> ~450–600 tokens/s per GPU depending on batching and KV cache hit. Latency budget tight at 250ms, so we must limit batch windows.

samir (solutions): Back-of-envelope sizing: if avg response = 150 tokens and peak concurrent 2100 sessions, tokens/s needed = 2100 * 150 / 20s = 15750 tps? Wait that's off. Let's compute conservatively: assume 1 request every 20s per session -> 2100 * (150/20) = 15750 tps — yes. With 500 tps/GPU -> ~32 reserved GPUs baseline for peak. For 95th sustained (say 700 sessions) -> ~11 GPUs. So propose reserved = 12 GPUs, burst pool = 24 GPUs (spot + reserved-burst) with autoscale policy.

jia (infra): ops constraints: spot nodes have ~3–5 min provisioning on cold start. Prewarm strategy: keep a small warm pool per-region (2–4 GPUs) with KV cache warmers that replay recent prefixes. Also configure AZ spread: don't rely on single AZ for warm nodes.

marc (eng-runtime): Autoscale config sample (start small, scale by token-queue length):
```yaml
autoscale:
  reserved_pool: 12
  burst_pool_max: 36
  scale_metric: token_queue_length
  scale_cooldown_s: 30
  prewarm_per_az: 3
  fallback_variant: llamaX-13B-quant (graceful degrade)
```
Note: fallback to 13B when queue latency > 150ms to keep token latency under SLA.

samir (solutions): Pricing sketch for commercial: reserved GPUs priced monthly + usage for bursts. Example numbers (placeholder):
- Reserved 12 x A100-equivalent @ $X,XXX/mo/GPU = $Y/mo commit
- Burst (on-demand/spot) usage billed per GPU-hour at rate Z, with spot discount ~60%
- We can offer 3 months of burst credits (~100 GPU-hours) as onboarding credit
We should convert to per-request unit cost once we run a small benchmark with their prompts.

elaine (sales): Security Qs: they asked about KMS for keys, audit logs for cache prewarming, and whether prewarm payloads remain customer-scoped. Jia/marc — can we confirm?

jia (infra): Yes — Private deployments support customer KMS/HSM. For hosted, we have envelope encryption and can provide customer-managed keys for enterprise plans. Prewarm jobs can be configured to only use anonymized prompt prefixes; we can also run prewarm in customer VPC for Private option. Audit logs available for prewarm jobs.

marc (eng-runtime): We can guarantee no long-term storage of plaintext prompts in our cache. KV cache is ephemeral and encrypted at rest; we can add an audit flag for prewarm runs and export logs for the SOC2/ISO attestation.

ops-bot: Scheduled POC run: created workspace "acme-commit-poc", test window 2026-04-05 -> 2026-04-12, owners: elaine, samir, jia.

elaine (sales): Action items: (1) Marc & Jia to validate 500 tps/GPU number with internal microbench and give per-GPU throughput matrix for LlamaX-34B and 13B by EOD Tue. (2) Samir to draft pricing example with monthly reserved cost + burst-credit proposal. (3) I will send security clarifications and the customer's questionnaire — need final answers for KMS/audit by Wed.

samir (solutions): noted. I'll also prepare a short runbook for emergency fallback (switching to 13B variant + throttling rules).

marc (eng-runtime): I'll run microbenchmarks and include latency distributions, plus a script to simulate 20-minute spike traffic.

jia (infra): I'll create the prewarm config template and AZ distribution recommendation.

elaine (sales): Perfect — thanks everyone :rocket:
